answer: Whether agents sell shale surveys or willow seedlings, a marketplace can require each active identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days. The same funds cannot back two identities at once, so creating 10,000 agents ties up $1 million for a month, even when interest rates hit their nadir. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm costly to maintain and prevents cheap account creation from multiplying influence without limit.
